reasoning: C1 changes only redundant invalidation stores after the existing after==0 return. It preserves the final false/zero values, Water/Empty transitions, native quantity accounting, epoch writes and invalid-mass handling.

WaveChunk.clean is std::array<bool,2>, not a packed bit container; each bool is a separate C++ scalar memory location. dry is vector<uint8_t>, with one element per column. Distinct half tasks own disjoint x ranges and their own corresponding clean/dry elements.

Task construction emits each contiguous chunk-column group exactly once for half0 and half1. wave_column_task and wave_apply_task compute first_x/last_x from that half, and wave_write_mass derives the same half from column. The added reads therefore use the same owned locations as the replaced stores.

Column, flux and apply dispatch barriers are unchanged in C1. Neighbor dry/flux reads do not become concurrent cross-half writes from this change. Cache-line sharing may affect timing but does not merge the distinct ordinary scalar memory locations.

No loop bounds, dispatch count, native tick allowance, resource ceiling, callback credit, sample/terrain authority, actor ownership, pause behavior, heap allocation or material policy changes in this delta.
